_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `Puzzle2dMutation` is a semio-NATIVE vocabulary carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no oracle is registered and the decision below records what stands in for one.

oracles.rationale: A second implementation of the `s.puzzle.2d` board document and its twenty-six typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-puzzle-2d-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️component.json` (the five members), rules 2, 4 and 7 of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md`, and the twenty-six committed `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintets — which are the only statement of four things: that a node's handle list is INSIDE the node, so removing a handle is a node mutation that CASCADES into the edges attached to it; that deleting a node severs every edge attached to any of its handles; that `replace-node-geometry` rebuilds shape and extent from four arguments and drops every member whose argument is null; and that a member equal to its default is OMITTED from the carrier. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. This registration SUPERSEDES the `puzzle-2d-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision, whose argument — that handles living inside nodes while edges are a sibling collection "is this subset's own specification, not a fact an external diagram or graph library could confirm or refute" — was refuted in this same wave by `mutate-fem2d-1` and `mutate-gismap-1`, which took Python second implementations over this same carrier; a two-level connectivity is not an obstacle to a second implementation, it is something a second implementation must model, and this one models both cascades. A THIRD-PARTY library was declined, not merely absent: GraphML, DOT and GEXF all join node to node and none of them can express an edge whose endpoints are ports OWNED BY a node, let alone read this carrier. THE REFERENCE REFUSES TWO OF THE FIFTY-THREE SCENARIOS BY CLAUSE, and says so in role. First, `replace-node-handle` (both roles): its single committed vector supplies a genuinely different handle — `handle-1` moves from `handle-kind-a` to `handle-kind-c` — yet its committed outcome declares `mutation.no-op` and its after-snapshot is identical to its before-snapshot. Three different rules produce exactly that and no committed document distinguishes them: the verb is unimplemented, or it refuses a handle an edge is attached to (which `handle-1` is), or it refuses a kind the compatibility relation does not admit (which `handle-kind-c` is). One more vector, on an unconnected handle, decides it. Second, `inverse-replace-kind-catalogs`: the committed vector INSTALLS a catalogue where the before-snapshot had none, so undoing it requires removing the member, and nothing states whether the verb accepts a null argument. A FINDING THE REFERENCE MADE WHILE BEING WRITTEN: this subset's `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🔣️component.json` is not a mutation schema at all — it is titled `Puzzle2dMutation` but declares `{schema, camera, nodes, edges, meta}`, a copy of the SNAPSHOT schema, and is the pre-migration whole-snapshot-shaped generic schema that `s.architect.program`'s own mutation schema records itself as superseding. It was never replaced here, so the verbs and their argument lists had to be read off the committed payloads instead. ONE CEILING ON WHAT THIS COMPARISON ESTABLISHES: the SUBJECT half does not run this subset's codec — `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-puzzle-2d-1/🦀️component.rs` links no plugin crate and replays the committed vectors — so today it establishes that an independent implementation of the specification computes the committed after-snapshots, not yet our codec against a second producer. A `puzzle2d_mutation_report_json` bridge beside the mutation enum closes it; it is not added here for two reasons, and neither is that the verb is hard: it is PRODUCTION code in a crate this test-side pass deliberately does not touch, and it could not be verified end to end today anyway. `parity` was not measured for any case in this pass: the single-case probe `parity exhaustive --owner 🗒️note --case mutate-note-1` was killed at the runner's OWN 900 s per-case budget while still COMPILING the generated subject host — the runner's message names the cause, shared cargo target-dir lock contention from a concurrent session — and then threw `spawnSync cargo ETIMEDOUT` out of `runProbe` with no summary line at all. `📓️w14-final-audit.md` §5.3 measured the underlying blocker one day earlier (`unresolved import component::component_persistent_local` in `semio-framework-plugin`, which sits in every generated host's dependency graph); this pass did NOT re-verify whether that is still the state, and says so rather than repeating it as fact. This subset's own plugin crate compiles clean at `cargo check --lib`. This case also reads no real-world artifact: all 130 of its fixtures are handcrafted specification vectors. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.
